A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aging is characterized by a progressive attenuation of GnRH/LH feedforward drive and an increasingly robust androgen negative feedback inhibition.
the hypothalamo-piutitary axis is not as responsive in older men as in younger men.
the aging male has a relative hypogonadal state that is due to a reduction in GnRH/LH pulse amplitude, which in turn, is due to a decrease in GnRH pulse amplitude.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aging men have a reduced GnRH drive, and this reduced drive is not compensated by an increase in LH secretion.
, in healthy older males, a diminished amplitude of endogenous pulsatile LH secretion is not simply due to a reduced GnRH drive but also reflects impaired GnRH/LH neuroregulatory reserve

the neuroendocrine control of LH secretion is compromised in older men, even when serum testosterone concentrations are normal, and that these age-related defects can be unmasked by experimental suppression of endogenous androgen biosynthesis.
